intent.raw_query: Nepal trekking Annapurna, $2000 solo, October 2026, 14 days

experiences.name: Annapurna Base Camp Trek
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic multi-day trek to Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130m, passing through rhododendron forests, traditional Gurung villages, and dramatic mountain landscapes with stunning views of Annapurna I, Machapuchare, and Hiunchuli peaks.

experiences.name: Poon Hill Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Rise before dawn and hike to Poon Hill viewpoint at 3,210m for one of the most spectacular Himalayan panoramas in Nepal, watching the golden sunrise illuminate the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri mountain ranges in breathtaking alpenglow colors.

experiences.name: Gurung Village Cultural Walk in Ghandruk
experiences.description: Explore the beautifully preserved Gurung village of Ghandruk, visiting the Gurung Museum, interacting with local families, observing traditional stone-paved pathways, and learning about indigenous culture, customs, and the history of Gurkha soldiers.

experiences.name: Mardi Himal Trek and High Camp Exploration
experiences.description: Trek the less-crowded Mardi Himal trail through dense bamboo and rhododendron forests to High Camp at 3,580m, enjoying close-up views of Machapuchare (Fishtail Mountain) and Mardi Himal with far fewer trekkers than the main Annapurna circuit.

experiences.name: Jhinu Danda Natural Hot Springs Soak
experiences.description: After days of strenuous trekking, descend to the natural hot springs at Jhinu Danda along the Modi Khola river. Soak in geothermal mineral pools surrounded by lush jungle and listen to the rushing river below, offering the perfect natural recovery experience for tired trekking muscles.
experiences.location: Jhinu Danda, Modi Khola River Valley

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Annapurna, Nepal
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 13:00. Complete immigration and baggage claim. Take a budget pre-paid taxi or shared bus from the airport to Pokhara (or arrange onward transport toward Annapurna region). Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Rest and freshen up after the long journey. Take a short orientation walk around the immediate resort area to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the nearby lakeside or village area to soak in the Annapurna atmosphere. Watch the sunset over the Himalayas if weather permits. Explore local tea stalls and small shops near the resort.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab a quick snack at the airport — budget NPR 200–400
meals.lunch: Dal Bhat (lentil soup with rice) at a local teahouse near the resort — budget NPR 300–500
meals.dinner: Thakali set meal (traditional Nepali cuisine) at a local diner near the resort — budget NPR 400–600

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is primarily a travel and acclimatization day. Do not overexert yourself. Stay hydrated. Exchange currency at the airport or a local money changer for better rates. Keep NPR cash on hand as ATMs can be scarce in trekking areas.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning yoga or light stretching at the resort to acclimatize. After breakfast, visit the Pokhara lakeside (Phewa Lake) area — enjoy a peaceful walk along the lake shore and take in views of the Annapurna range reflected in the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a wooden rowboat on Phewa Lake (NPR 300–500/hour) and paddle to the Tal Barahi Temple on the island in the middle of the lake. Explore the temple and enjoy panoramic mountain views. Return to shore and visit the Tibetan Refugee Camp at Tashiling for a cultural experience and browse handmade crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Old Bazaar in Pokhara for local shopping and people-watching. Enjoy the vibrant atmosphere of Lakeside (Baidam) area as vendors and trekkers mingle.

meals.breakfast: Porridge or eggs with toast at the resort or a nearby café — budget NPR 200–350
meals.lunch: Momos (dumplings) and butter tea at a Tibetan café near the refugee camp — budget NPR 250–400
meals.dinner: Nepali thali or vegetable curry at a local restaurant in Lakeside area — budget NPR 400–600

day_by_day.notes: This is an acclimatization and orientation day. Pokhara sits at approximately 822m elevation. Avoid alcohol and heavy meals to help your body adjust. Purchase any missing trekking gear at Lakeside shops — prices are reasonable.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up before dawn and hire a local taxi or shared jeep to Sarangkot Hill (NPR 300–500 shared). Witness the spectacular sunrise over the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri mountain ranges — one of Nepal's most iconic views. Optionally try paragliding (budget operators offer NPR 5,000–7,000 for a 30-minute tandem flight).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Pokhara and visit the International Mountain Museum (entry NPR 300) to learn about Himalayan mountaineering history, local culture, and the Annapurna massif. Great preparation for your upcoming trek.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) — hike up or take a boat across Phewa Lake and then a short climb. Enjoy panoramic 360-degree views of Pokhara and the Himalayas at golden hour.

meals.breakfast: Pack a snack bar or banana for the pre-dawn Sarangkot trip. Proper breakfast after return — egg sandwich and tea at a local bakery — budget NPR 200–300
meals.lunch: Dal Bhat at a local teahouse near the museum — budget NPR 300–500
meals.dinner: Grilled vegetables and rice or pasta at a budget restaurant in Lakeside — budget NPR 400–600

day_by_day.notes: Bring a warm jacket for the pre-dawn Sarangkot visit — temperatures can drop significantly before sunrise even in October. Confirm your trekking permits and TIMS card today if not already arranged. ACAP permit costs NPR 3,000 and TIMS card costs NPR 2,000 for foreign nationals.

day_by_day.morning: Obtain your ACAP (Annapurna Conservation Area Permit) and TIMS (Trekkers' Information Management System) card at the Nepal Tourism Board office in Pokhara if not done already. Pack your trekking bag — keep it light (under 10kg). Take a local bus or shared jeep to Nayapul (NPR 200–300, approximately 1.5 hours). Begin the iconic Annapurna Base Camp or Poon Hill trek. Trek from Nayapul to Tikhedhunga (approximately 3–4 hours, 1,540m elevation).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking through terraced rice fields, rhododendron forests, and small Gurung villages. Arrive at Tikhedhunga teahouse area. Check in to a basic teahouse (NPR 200–400/night — rooms are often free or cheap if you eat at the teahouse).
day_by_day.evening: Rest legs, journal, and mingle with fellow trekkers at the teahouse. Enjoy the peaceful mountain village atmosphere. Watch the stars from the teahouse terrace if skies are clear.

meals.breakfast: Porridge with honey and tea at the resort before departure — budget NPR 200–300
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at a trail-side teahouse for noodle soup — budget NPR 300–500
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat at the Tikhedhunga teahouse — budget NPR 400–600 (often unlimited refills!)

day_by_day.notes: October is peak trekking season — trails will be busy but teahouses will be fully operational. Always drink boiled or filtered water (NPR 50–100/bottle at teahouses). Start trekking early each day to avoid afternoon cloud cover that often rolls in. Trekking poles are highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Early start from Tikhedhunga. Trek the famous stone staircase climb to Ulleri (approximately 3,280 steps — challenging but rewarding). The ascent takes about 1.5–2 hours. Enjoy spectacular views of the Modi Khola valley and surrounding peaks. Continue through oak and rhododendron forest to Banthanti.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Banthanti to Ghorepani (2,860m elevation) — approximately 4–5 hours total from Tikhedhunga. Ghorepani is a bustling trekking hub with many teahouses. Check in and rest. Explore the small village and enjoy views of Dhaulagiri and Annapurna South.
day_by_day.evening: Warm up by the teahouse fire or wood stove — evenings at 2,860m are cool in October. Meet other trekkers and share trail stories. Early to bed as tomorrow requires a very early start.

meals.breakfast: Tibetan bread with jam and tea at Tikhedhunga teahouse — budget NPR 200–350
meals.lunch: Vegetable noodle soup or fried rice at a Banthanti teahouse — budget NPR 300–500
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat or pasta with vegetables at Ghorepani teahouse — budget NPR 400–600

day_by_day.notes: The Ulleri staircase is steep — take your time and rest frequently. Altitude increases significantly today. Drink plenty of water and avoid alcohol. If you feel symptoms of altitude sickness (headache, nausea, dizziness), rest and do not ascend further. Ghorepani has charging facilities for a small fee (NPR 100–200).

day_by_day.morning: Wake up at 4:30–5:00 AM. Trek 45 minutes to 1 hour to Poon Hill (3,210m) in the dark with a headlamp. Watch one of the most spectacular sunrises in the world over the Annapurna range — Annapurna I, II, III, IV, Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), Dhaulagiri, and more are visible. Return to Ghorepani for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek from Ghorepani to Tadapani (approximately 4–5 hours through beautiful rhododendron and magnolia forests). The trail offers continued spectacular mountain views. Arrive at Tadapani (2,630m) and check in to a teahouse.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the teahouse and enjoy the quieter, less-crowded atmosphere of Tadapani compared to Ghorepani. Watch the alpenglow on the peaks at sunset. Rest your legs for tomorrow's trek.

meals.breakfast: Hot lemon tea on Poon Hill (vendors set up early — NPR 100–150), then proper breakfast back at Ghorepani — eggs, toast, and tea — budget NPR 250–400
meals.lunch: Packed snacks or stop at a trail teahouse for soup — budget NPR 300–500
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat or vegetable curry at Tadapani teahouse — budget NPR 400–600

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill entry fee is NPR 100. Bring your warmest layer for the pre-dawn Poon Hill hike — temperatures can be near or below freezing at this elevation in October. The sunrise here is considered one of the top 10 sunrise experiences in the world. Do not miss it!

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tadapani toward Chhomrong (2,170m) — approximately 4–5 hours. The trail descends steeply through dense forest before climbing back up to Chhomrong, a large and well-equipped Gurung village. Enjoy views of Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain) and Annapurna South.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Chhomrong and check in to a teahouse. Explore the village — visit the local school and interact with the friendly Gurung community. Chhomrong is the last major village before the Annapurna Sanctuary and has good facilities. Stock up on snacks and supplies for the higher altitude sections ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a well-earned rest at the teahouse. The views of Machhapuchhre from Chhomrong at sunset are absolutely stunning. Review your permits and plan the next few days of trekking toward Annapurna Base Camp.

meals.breakfast: Porridge with banana and honey at Tadapani teahouse — budget NPR 200–350
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or fried rice at a trail teahouse — budget NPR 300–500
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat (unlimited) at Chhomrong teahouse — budget NPR 400–600

day_by_day.notes: Today marks the halfway point of your trek. Your body should be well-acclimatized by now. Chhomrong has a checkpoint where your ACAP permit will be checked. Make sure to carry your permits at all times. The stone staircase in Chhomrong is long and tiring — take it slow.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong down the stone steps to Sinuwa and continue through bamboo and rhododendron forest to Bamboo (2,310m) — approximately 3 hours. The trail follows the Modi Khola river and the scenery becomes increasingly dramatic as the valley narrows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from Bamboo to Dovan (2,600m) — approximately 2 more hours through dense bamboo groves. The trail is relatively flat and beautiful. Arrive at Dovan and check in to a teahouse. The area is known for occasional wildlife sightings including Himalayan Tahr and various bird species.
day_by_day.evening: Relax and rest at the Dovan teahouse. The sound of the Modi Khola river rushing below creates a soothing atmosphere. Prepare mentally and physically for the higher altitude push tomorrow. Drink plenty of fluids and eat a good dinner.

meals.breakfast: Tibetan bread with peanut butter and tea at Chhomrong — budget NPR 200–350
meals.lunch: Garlic soup (excellent for altitude acclimatization) and bread at Bamboo teahouse — budget NPR 300–500
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat or pasta at Dovan teahouse — budget NPR 400–600

day_by_day.notes: Garlic soup is a trekker's staple and is believed to help with altitude acclimatization — order it at every opportunity above 2,500m. The bamboo forest section is magical but can be slippery when wet. Wear good grip trekking boots. Watch for leeches on the trail in damp conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Early start from Dovan. Trek through Himalaya Hotel (2,920m) and continue to Hinku Cave (3,170m) and then Deurali (3,230m). The landscape becomes more alpine and dramatic. Snow-capped peaks begin to tower overhead. Approximately 4–5 hours of trekking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the final push from Deurali to Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) at 3,700m — approximately 2–3 hours. The trail enters the Annapurna Sanctuary — a glacial amphitheater surrounded by some of the world's highest peaks. The views become truly awe-inspiring. Check in to a teahouse at MBC.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from MBC — the golden light on Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, and Gangapurna is absolutely breathtaking. Take photos and simply absorb the magnificent scenery. Go to bed early for tomorrow's early ABC push.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and tea at Dovan — budget NPR 200–350
meals.lunch: Hot soup and bread at Himalaya Hotel teahouse — budget NPR 350–550
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat or noodles at MBC teahouse — budget NPR 500–700 (prices increase with altitude)

day_by_day.notes: You are now at 3,700m elevation. Altitude sickness risk increases significantly. Walk slowly, breathe deeply, and drink 3–4 liters of water today. If you experience severe headache, vomiting, or difficulty breathing, descend immediately. Do not ascend if you feel unwell. The Annapurna Sanctuary is a sacred and protected area — do not litter.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up at 5:00 AM. Trek the final 2 hours from MBC to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) at 4,130m. Arrive at ABC for sunrise — one of the most profound experiences available to trekkers anywhere in the world. You are surrounded by a 360-degree wall of Himalayan giants: Annapurna I (8,091m — 10th highest in the world), Annapurna South, Machhapuchhre, Hiunchuli, Gangapurna, and more.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend time at ABC exploring the area, taking photos, and absorbing the incredible atmosphere. Visit the memorials to climbers who have lost their lives on Annapurna — the world's deadliest 8,000m peak by fatality rate. Begin descent back to MBC and continue to Deurali or Himalaya Hotel teahouse.
day_by_day.evening: Continue descending to Bamboo or Dovan if energy allows — descending is much faster than ascending. Rest at whichever teahouse you reach. Celebrate your achievement of reaching Annapurna Base Camp!

meals.breakfast: Energy bars and hot tea before the ABC push — budget NPR 100–200
meals.lunch: Hot soup and noodles at ABC teahouse — budget NPR 500–800 (highest prices on the trek)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat at Himalaya Hotel or Bamboo teahouse on descent — budget NPR 400–600

day_by_day.notes: This is the highlight of the entire trip — the culmination of days of trekking. Take your time at ABC and do not rush. The descent from ABC to MBC to Bamboo in one day is achievable and recommended to get back to lower altitude quickly. Knees take significant strain on descent — trekking poles are very helpful.

day_by_day.morning: Continue descent from your overnight stop (Bamboo or Dovan) back through Sinuwa to Chhomrong — approximately 4–5 hours. Your body will feel the accumulated fatigue of the trek but the descent is manageable. Enjoy the changing vegetation as you drop back into rhododendron and oak forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: From Chhomrong, continue descending to Jhinu Danda (1,760m) — approximately 1.5 hours further. Jhinu Danda has natural hot springs along the Modi Khola river. Soak your tired trekking legs in the hot springs (entry fee NPR 200–300) — an absolute treat after days of hard trekking.
day_by_day.evening: Stay overnight at a Jhinu Danda teahouse. Enjoy a relaxed evening by the river. Reflect on the incredible journey of the past week. The hot spring soak will work wonders on tired muscles.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and tea at your overnight teahouse — budget NPR 200–350
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or fried rice at a Chhomrong teahouse — budget NPR 300–500
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat or vegetable curry at Jhinu Danda teahouse — budget NPR 400–600

day_by_day.notes: The Jhinu Danda hot springs are one of the most rewarding experiences on the entire Annapurna Circuit — do not skip them! The springs are a 20-minute walk down steep steps from the village to the river. Go in the late afternoon for the best experience. Bring a towel and flip flops.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Jhinu Danda back to Nayapul via Kimche — approximately 4–5 hours through terraced farmland and small villages. This is a gentle, mostly downhill trail through beautiful rural Nepal. Enjoy the lush green landscapes and local farm life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Nayapul and take a local bus or shared jeep back to Pokhara (NPR 200–300, approximately 1.5 hours). Check back in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Take a long hot shower — one of the best showers of your life after days on the trail! Rest and do laundry.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the successful completion of your Annapurna trek with a proper sit-down dinner at a Pokhara restaurant. Browse Lakeside area for souvenirs — Pashmina scarves, Thangka paintings, trekking gear, and local crafts make great gifts.

meals.breakfast: Egg and toast with tea at Jhinu Danda teahouse — budget NPR 200–350
meals.lunch: Packed snacks on the trail or stop at a village teahouse — budget NPR 200–400
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner! Try a proper Nepali restaurant in Lakeside — Newari cuisine or mixed grill — budget NPR 600–900

day_by_day.notes: You have completed an incredible multi-day Himalayan trek — congratulations! Take care of any blisters or minor injuries. Visit a pharmacy in Pokhara if needed. Back in Pokhara, ATMs are available and you can restock cash. Consider tipping your teahouse hosts — even NPR 200–500 per teahouse is greatly appreciated.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a well-deserved rest morning at the resort. Sleep in and have a leisurely breakfast. Visit the Gupteshwor Mahadev Cave (entry NPR 100) near Davis Falls — a sacred Hindu cave with a natural underground waterfall. Also visit Davis Falls (Patale Chhango) nearby — a dramatic waterfall that disappears underground.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Bindabasini Temple — the oldest temple in Pokhara and an important Hindu site. Explore the surrounding market area. In the afternoon, consider a visit to the Annapurna Butterfly Museum or simply relax by Phewa Lake with a good book and a cup of Himalayan tea.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening stroll along the Lakeside promenade. Browse the night market stalls. Enjoy a cultural performance if available at a local restaurant (some Lakeside restaurants offer traditional Nepali dance shows). Pack your bags for departure.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the resort or a Lakeside café — eggs, toast, fresh juice, and coffee — budget NPR 300–500
meals.lunch: Chatamari (Newari rice crepe) and local snacks at the Old Bazaar — budget NPR 200–400
meals.dinner: Goodbye Nepal dinner — try Thakali cuisine (the regional food of the Annapurna area) at a local restaurant — budget NPR 500–700

day_by_day.notes: This is your recovery and cultural exploration day. Your body needs rest after the intense trekking. Avoid strenuous activity. If you want one last adventure, consider a short sunrise hike to Sarangkot or a paragliding session over Phewa Lake. Visit the Nepal Tourism Board office to provide feedback on your trekking experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Annapurna/Pokhara region. Wake up early for one last sunrise view of the Annapurna range from the resort or lakeside. Take a final peaceful walk along Phewa Lake. Pack all belongings and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange transport back to Kathmandu — options include tourist bus (NPR 800–1,200, 6–7 hours), local bus (NPR 400–600, 7–8 hours), or domestic flight (NPR 8,000–15,000, 25 minutes — splurge option for last day). If flying home from Kathmandu, allow at least 3–4 hours before your flight. If you have time in Kathmandu, visit Thamel district for last-minute shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Nepal with incredible memories of the Himalayas, the warmth of the Nepali people, and the achievement of trekking to Annapurna Base Camp. Final airport meal or snack before your flight home.

meals.breakfast: Final Nepali breakfast — sel roti (ring-shaped rice bread) with yogurt and tea at a local spot — budget NPR 150–300
meals.lunch: Snack on the bus or at a roadside stop en route to Kathmandu — budget NPR 200–400
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or Thamel restaurant for a final meal — budget NPR 500–800

day_by_day.notes: Namaste and safe travels! Nepal will stay in your heart forever. Final budget summary reminder: ACAP Permit NPR 3,000, TIMS Card NPR 2,000, daily teahouse accommodation NPR 200–400/night, daily meals NPR 1,000–2,000/day on trek, local transport NPR 200–500 per segment. Total estimated trip budget (excluding flights): USD 400–600 for 14 days — excellent value for a once-in-a-lifetime Himalayan adventure.

trip_options.title: Classic Annapurna, Nepal Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at destination — flight lands at 13:00, so no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from airport to Aegean Bliss Resort, Pokhara/Annapurna region. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation walk around the resort grounds and nearby lakeside area to get acquainted with your surroundings. Enjoy views of the Annapurna massif from the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Phewa Lake promenade near the resort, watch the sunset reflect off the lake with Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain) in the backdrop. Explore the local Lakeside (Baidam) bazaar area gently.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the resort's café or a nearby local eatery upon arrival — try dal bhat (lentil soup with rice) for around NPR 300–500
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort restaurant or a well-regarded Lakeside restaurant such as Moondance Restaurant — try Nepali thali set meal, budget NPR 800–1,200

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Pokhara sits at ~820m elevation, so no acclimatization concerns yet. Confirm any trekking permits (TIMS card, ACAP permit) needed for upcoming days. Rest well for the adventure ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Early rise for sunrise at Sarangkot Hill (1,592m) — either hire a taxi or join a shared jeep from Lakeside. Arrive before 6:00 AM for a breathtaking panoramic view of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges glowing in the first light. One of Nepal's most iconic sunrise spots.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Pokhara and visit the International Mountain Museum — a world-class museum dedicated to the Himalayas, its people, flora, and the history of mountaineering expeditions. Spend 2–3 hours exploring exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Boat ride on Phewa Lake (rowboat rental ~NPR 500/hour) and visit the Tal Barahi Temple on a small island in the middle of the lake. Return before dusk and explore the Lakeside night market.

meals.breakfast: Light snack at a Sarangkot tea house — egg sandwich and milk tea, NPR 200–350
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant near the museum — try momo (dumplings) and vegetable curry, NPR 400–600
meals.dinner: Dinner at Caffe Concerto or similar mid-range Lakeside restaurant — pasta, pizza, or Nepali dishes, NPR 700–1,100

day_by_day.notes: Sarangkot taxi costs approximately NPR 800–1,200 one way. Bring a warm jacket for the early morning hilltop — October mornings can be chilly at elevation. Museum entry fee approximately NPR 300 for foreigners.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the Poon Hill Trek preparation day — travel by local bus or shared jeep from Pokhara to Nayapul (1.5–2 hours, ~NPR 200–400). Start trekking from Nayapul to Tikhedhunga (1,540m), approximately 3–4 hours of moderate walking through terraced farmland and small villages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Tikhedhunga up the famous stone staircase to Ulleri (1,960m) — a steep but rewarding 1.5–2 hour climb with stunning valley views. Arrive at your teahouse in Ulleri and rest.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into a mid-range teahouse in Ulleri. Enjoy the tranquil mountain village atmosphere, interact with local Magar community members, and watch the stars emerge over the Himalayan ridgeline.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departure — porridge, eggs, toast, NPR 400–600
meals.lunch: Dal bhat at a teahouse in Tikhedhunga, NPR 350–500
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ulleri teahouse — dal bhat, vegetable noodle soup, or pasta, NPR 400–600 (teahouse meals are simple but hearty)

day_by_day.notes: Ensure you have your TIMS card and ACAP permit before starting the trek (obtainable in Pokhara, ~NPR 2,000–3,000 combined). Pack light — carry only a daypack if you hire a porter. October weather is generally excellent: clear skies, mild temperatures.

day_by_day.morning: Early start from Ulleri — trek to Ghorepani (2,860m), approximately 3–4 hours through beautiful rhododendron and oak forests. The trail climbs steadily with rewarding views opening up as you gain altitude. Arrive at Ghorepani by late morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drop your bags at the teahouse and hike up to Poon Hill (3,210m) for an afternoon preview of the panoramic views — Dhaulagiri (8,167m), Annapurna South (7,219m), Hiunchuli, and Machhapuchhre all visible. Return to Ghorepani.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the Ghorepani teahouse, warm up by the common room fire. Socialize with fellow trekkers from around the world. Set your alarm for 4:30 AM for the next morning's sunrise.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Ulleri teahouse — porridge with honey, boiled eggs, tea, NPR 300–450
meals.lunch: Lunch at a teahouse en route or in Ghorepani — veg fried rice or noodle soup, NPR 350–500
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ghorepani teahouse — dal bhat with seasonal vegetables, NPR 450–650

day_by_day.notes: Ghorepani sits at 2,860m — some trekkers may feel mild altitude symptoms. Drink plenty of water and avoid alcohol. Teahouse accommodation in Ghorepani costs approximately NPR 300–600/night per room (often free or discounted if you eat at the teahouse).

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn hike to Poon Hill (3,210m) — depart teahouse at 5:00 AM with a headlamp for the 45-minute climb. Witness one of the most spectacular sunrises in the Himalayas as golden light illuminates the entire Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. Return to Ghorepani for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek from Ghorepani to Tadapani (2,630m) via Deurali, approximately 4–5 hours through dense rhododendron forests — one of the most beautiful forest trails in the Annapurna region. Arrive at Tadapani teahouse.
day_by_day.evening: Evening views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli from Tadapani — the village offers some of the most intimate close-up Himalayan views on the circuit. Enjoy a quiet evening at the teahouse.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Ghorepani teahouse after returning from Poon Hill — eggs, toast, porridge, hot lemon tea, NPR 350–500
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or teahouse stop en route — apple pancakes (Annapurna region is famous for apple products), NPR 300–450
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tadapani teahouse — dal bhat or pasta, NPR 400–600

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill entry fee: NPR 100. The Ghorepani–Tadapani trail can be muddy in spots even in October — trekking poles recommended. Tadapani is a quieter, less commercialized village compared to Ghorepani.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tadapani to Chomrong (2,170m), approximately 4–5 hours descending through forests and crossing suspension bridges over the Modi Khola river. Chomrong is a beautiful Gurung village and the gateway to the Annapurna Sanctuary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Chomrong village — visit the local gompa (Buddhist monastery), interact with Gurung community members, and enjoy extraordinary views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli looming directly above the village.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset views from Chomrong are exceptional — the village sits on a ridge with 270-degree mountain panoramas. Enjoy a relaxed evening at a well-appointed teahouse (Chomrong has some of the better mid-range teahouses on this circuit).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Tadapani teahouse — muesli with milk, boiled eggs, tea, NPR 300–450
meals.lunch: Lunch at a teahouse en route — veg momos or noodle soup, NPR 350–500
meals.dinner: Dinner at Chomrong teahouse — try the local Gurung bread (roti) with lentil soup, or pasta, NPR 500–700

day_by_day.notes: Chomrong is a good rest point. If you feel fatigued, consider spending an extra half-day here before continuing. Chomrong has better facilities than villages further up — this is the last reliable place for hot showers and charging devices before the sanctuary.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chomrong toward the Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) trail — descend to Chhomrong Khola and ascend to Sinuwa (2,360m), then continue through bamboo and rhododendron forest to Bamboo (2,310m), approximately 3–4 hours total.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Bamboo to Dovan (2,600m) and on to Himalaya Hotel (2,920m), passing through increasingly dramatic gorge scenery with towering cliffs and the roaring Modi Khola river below. Approximately 3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Himalaya Hotel teahouse — a remote, cozy teahouse deep in the Annapurna gorge. The surrounding scenery is dramatic and otherworldly. Rest and prepare for the high-altitude push tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Chomrong teahouse — pancakes with honey, tea, NPR 350–500
meals.lunch: Lunch at Bamboo teahouse — dal bhat or fried rice, NPR 400–550
meals.dinner: Dinner at Himalaya Hotel teahouse — dal bhat (highly recommended for energy), NPR 450–650

day_by_day.notes: The Annapurna gorge trail can be prone to avalanche risk in winter months, but October is generally safe and ideal. Teahouse prices increase as you go higher — budget NPR 500–800 for meals at higher elevations. Stay hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Himalaya Hotel to Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC, 3,700m) via Deurali (3,230m), approximately 4–5 hours. The trail enters the Annapurna Sanctuary — a stunning glacial amphitheater surrounded by a ring of 7,000–8,000m peaks. The scenery becomes increasingly dramatic and surreal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from MBC to Annapurna Base Camp (4,130m), approximately 1.5–2 hours. Arrive at ABC and spend the afternoon taking in the extraordinary 360-degree panorama of Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Gangapurna, and Machhapuchhre.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Annapurna Base Camp — one of the most awe-inspiring experiences in the trekking world. The peaks turn shades of orange, pink, and purple as the sun sets. Spend the night at an ABC teahouse (basic but functional).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Himalaya Hotel — porridge, eggs, hot tea, NPR 400–550
meals.lunch: Lunch at MBC teahouse — simple noodle soup or dal bhat, NPR 500–700
meals.dinner: Dinner at ABC teahouse — dal bhat or pasta (limited menu at this altitude), NPR 600–800

day_by_day.notes: ABC sits at 4,130m — altitude sickness is a real concern. Ascend slowly, drink 3–4 liters of water daily, avoid alcohol, and descend immediately if you experience severe headache, vomiting, or confusion. October temperatures at ABC can drop to -5°C to -10°C at night — pack warm layers, gloves, and a good sleeping bag.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up at ABC for sunrise — the Annapurna massif illuminated by the first rays of sunlight is an unforgettable, once-in-a-lifetime spectacle. Spend the morning exploring the base camp area and taking photos of the surrounding glacier and peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin descent from ABC back toward Bamboo (2,310m) — descend via MBC, Deurali, and Himalaya Hotel, continuing all the way to Bamboo, approximately 5–6 hours of downhill trekking. Descending is significantly faster than ascending.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Bamboo teahouse, tired but elated. Celebrate your ABC achievement with fellow trekkers over a warm meal. The bamboo forest setting provides a peaceful contrast to the high-altitude drama of the past two days.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at ABC teahouse — hot porridge, tea, eggs, NPR 500–700
meals.lunch: Quick lunch at Himalaya Hotel en route — noodle soup, NPR 450–600
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bamboo teahouse — dal bhat with pickle and vegetables, NPR 400–600

day_by_day.notes: Descending quickly from 4,130m is generally safe and actually recommended for altitude acclimatization. Knees can take a beating on the long descent — use trekking poles and take your time on steep sections. Celebrate but rest well.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Bamboo back to Chomrong (2,170m), approximately 3–4 hours ascending through the bamboo and rhododendron forest. Enjoy the familiar trail with fresh eyes after your ABC achievement.
day_by_day.afternoon: From Chomrong, descend to Jhinu Danda (1,780m), approximately 1.5 hours. Jhinu Danda is famous for its natural hot springs — a perfect reward after days of hard trekking. Soak in the riverside hot springs (entry fee ~NPR 200) on the banks of the Modi Khola.
day_by_day.evening: Stay overnight at a teahouse in Jhinu Danda. The hot springs are also available in the evening for a second soak. Enjoy the relaxed, celebratory atmosphere among trekkers who have completed or are returning from ABC.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Bamboo teahouse — pancakes, tea, NPR 350–500
meals.lunch: Lunch at Chomrong teahouse — dal bhat or pasta, NPR 450–650
meals.dinner: Dinner at Jhinu Danda teahouse — veg curry with rice, apple pie (a local specialty), NPR 450–650

day_by_day.notes: The Jhinu Danda hot springs are a highlight of the Annapurna Sanctuary trek and should not be missed. The springs are located about 15 minutes' walk below the village. Bring a towel and flip-flops.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Jhinu Danda to New Bridge (1,340m), approximately 2 hours, then continue to Siwai and Nayapul (1,070m), approximately 2 more hours. This completes the Annapurna Sanctuary/Poon Hill circuit loop. Board a local bus or shared jeep back to Pokhara.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Pokhara by early afternoon. Return to Aegean Bliss Resort, check in, shower, and decompress. Treat yourself to a traditional Nepali massage or spa treatment at the resort or a nearby wellness center (approximately NPR 1,500–2,500 for a full-body massage).
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner in Pokhara's Lakeside district to mark the completion of your Annapurna trek. Explore the vibrant evening atmosphere of Lakeside with its restaurants, cafes, and souvenir shops.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Jhinu Danda teahouse — eggs, toast, tea, NPR 350–500
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nayapul before boarding transport — dal bhat or momo, NPR 300–450
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at a quality Lakeside restaurant — try Nepali set dinner with local wine or Everest beer, NPR 1,000–1,500

day_by_day.notes: Bus from Nayapul to Pokhara costs approximately NPR 150–200; shared jeep NPR 300–400. You've completed a challenging and rewarding trek — take the afternoon to genuinely rest and recover. Consider getting your trekking certificate stamped at the TIMS office in Pokhara.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the resort. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and relax by the resort grounds. Optional: gentle yoga or stretching session to ease sore muscles. Visit the Pokhara Regional Museum or the Gurkha Memorial Museum for cultural enrichment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a half-day excursion to the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) — a stunning white Buddhist stupa perched on a hilltop south of Phewa Lake with panoramic views of Pokhara, the lake, and the Annapurna range. Reach it by boat across the lake and a 30-minute hike up, or by taxi.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset viewing from the World Peace Pagoda or return to Lakeside for sunset over Phewa Lake. Visit a local cultural show featuring traditional Nepali and Gurung folk dances (several venues in Lakeside offer evening performances, ~NPR 500–800).

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the resort — eggs your way, toast, fruit, juice, coffee, NPR 600–900
meals.lunch: Café lunch near the museum or Lakeside — try yak cheese sandwich, fresh juice, NPR 500–700
meals.dinner: Dinner at a Lakeside rooftop restaurant with lake views — mixed grill or Nepali thali, NPR 900–1,300

day_by_day.notes: World Peace Pagoda boat + entry: approximately NPR 500–700 total. This is a well-deserved rest day — don't over-schedule. Let your body recover fully before any remaining activities. October evenings in Pokhara are pleasantly cool (~15–18°C).

day_by_day.morning: Day hike to Begnas Lake and Rupa Lake — located about 15km east of Pokhara, these twin lakes offer a serene, less-touristy alternative to Phewa Lake. Hire a taxi or local bus to Begnas Bazaar and walk the trails around the lake through farmland and small villages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional adventure activity: paragliding over Pokhara and Phewa Lake from Sarangkot — Pokhara is one of the world's top paragliding destinations. Tandem paragliding flights cost approximately USD 80–100 (NPR 10,000–13,000) for a 30-minute flight with certified operators. Alternatively, visit the Seti River George for a dramatic natural gorge walk.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in the Pokhara/Annapurna region. Visit the Lakeside night market for souvenir shopping — trekking gear, pashmina scarves, thangka paintings, and handmade crafts make excellent souvenirs. Budget NPR 1,000–3,000 for shopping.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at resort or a Lakeside café — banana pancakes (a Pokhara classic), fresh fruit, tea, NPR 400–600
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch near Begnas Lake — pack food from a local bakery, or eat at a lakeside teahouse, NPR 300–500
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at one of Pokhara's best mid-range restaurants — try Lemon Tree or similar — Nepali/Continental fusion menu, NPR 1,000–1,500

day_by_day.notes: Paragliding is weather-dependent — October is generally excellent for flying with clear skies and good thermals. Book with a reputable operator (Sunrise Paragliding, Blue Sky Paragliding). Begnas Lake taxi: approximately NPR 800–1,200 round trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Annapurna/Pokhara. Wake up early for one last sunrise walk along Phewa Lake promenade — a peaceful, reflective way to close the journey. Pack your bags and check out of the resort. Visit a local tea house for a final cup of Nepali milk tea (chiya).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time: visit any remaining Pokhara attractions — the Devi's Fall (Patale Chhango), a spectacular waterfall that disappears underground, and the adjacent Gupteshwor Mahadev Cave (combined entry ~NPR 200). Transfer to Pokhara Airport for domestic flight to Kathmandu, or directly to Tribhuvan International Airport for international departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure or overnight in Kathmandu if flight schedule requires. If time permits in Kathmandu, visit Thamel district for a final Nepali meal and last-minute shopping before your international flight.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the resort or a Lakeside café — full Nepali breakfast with sel roti (traditional rice doughnuts), eggs, and chiya, NPR 400–600
meals.lunch: Light lunch before departure — momo at a local restaurant, NPR 300–450
meals.dinner: If departing: airport meal or in-flight dining. If overnighting in Kathmandu: dinner in Thamel at a classic Nepali restaurant — try Thakali kitchen for authentic mountain cuisine, NPR 800–1,200

day_by_day.notes: Pokhara to Kathmandu domestic flight: approximately USD 100–130 (book in advance). Allow 2–3 hours before domestic flight departure for check-in and security. Ensure all trekking permits are returned or retained as souvenirs. Nepal requires a valid visa — confirm return visa requirements for your nationality. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Annapurna, Nepal Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Kathmandu airport to Pokhara via scenic mountain highway or chartered helicopter flight over the Himalayas for breathtaking aerial views of Annapurna range. Check-in at Aegean Bliss Resort with a welcome refreshment ceremony and resort orientation tour.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into your premium suite, enjoy a relaxing sunset view of the Annapurna massif from your private terrace. Light stroll along the resort grounds to acclimatize to the altitude and fresh mountain air.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport lounge)
meals.lunch: Light refreshments provided during private transfer or at a premium stopover restaurant en route
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the resort's signature restaurant featuring Nepali fusion cuisine — try the dal bhat thali with locally sourced ingredients, paired with Himalayan herbal tea

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — keep activities minimal to combat jet lag and begin altitude acclimatization. Drink plenty of water and avoid strenuous activity.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided sunrise hike to a nearby viewpoint overlooking the Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain). Witness the golden alpenglow on snow-capped peaks with a personal mountain guide and hot thermos of Nepali tea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided nature walk through the lush rhododendron and oak forests surrounding the resort. Explore local flora and fauna with a naturalist guide, spotting Himalayan birds including the Danphe (Nepal's national bird). Visit a nearby traditional Gurung village for a cultural immersion experience.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxing evening at the resort's spa — indulge in a traditional Ayurvedic massage using Himalayan herbs and oils. Pre-dinner cocktails at the sky lounge with panoramic mountain views.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet mountain breakfast at the resort — fresh-baked bread, local honey, farm eggs, Himalayan granola, and premium Nepali coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by the resort chef enjoyed at a scenic forest clearing during the nature walk
meals.dinner: Fine dining at the resort restaurant — roasted lamb with mountain herbs, seasonal Himalayan vegetables, and a curated selection of international wines

day_by_day.notes: October is peak trekking season in Annapurna — expect clear skies and excellent visibility. Temperatures are mild during the day (15–22°C) and cooler at night (5–10°C). Layer appropriately.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day guided trek to Poon Hill (3,210m) — one of the most iconic viewpoints in the Annapurna region. Begin early morning ascent through Tikhedhunga and Ulleri with a private guide and luxury porter service. Stunning views of Dhaulagiri, Annapurna I, and Machhapuchhre.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend through charming Ghorepani village, exploring the local bazaar and interacting with Magar and Gurung communities. Visit a traditional teahouse for a cultural exchange experience before private vehicle return to resort.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort for a warm foot soak and recovery treatment at the spa. Enjoy a curated slideshow of the day's photography with a personal travel photographer's highlights.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-trek breakfast at resort — high-energy porridge, eggs, fresh fruit, and Nepali black tea
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch with sandwiches, energy bars, fresh fruit, and hot soup in a thermal flask enjoyed at Poon Hill summit
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at the resort — Nepali set menu with gundruk soup, sekuwa (grilled meats), and sel roti dessert, paired with local Khukri rum cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill trek is approximately 12–14 km round trip with 1,000m elevation gain. Difficulty is moderate. Luxury porter service is included — guests carry only day packs. Start by 5:30 AM for sunrise views.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the resort. Optional gentle yoga session on the mountain-view deck led by a certified Himalayan yoga instructor. Meditation session with a local Buddhist monk in the resort's dedicated mindfulness pavilion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat excursion on Phewa Lake in Pokhara — luxury wooden boat with personal guide. Visit the Tal Barahi Temple on the island in the middle of the lake. Explore the lakeside promenade and visit the International Mountain Museum for a premium guided tour of Himalayan history and mountaineering heritage.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a premium lakeside lounge in Pokhara's Lakeside district. Browse high-end Himalayan craft boutiques for cashmere, Thangka paintings, and hand-crafted jewelry.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at resort — eggs benedict, smoked salmon, fresh-pressed juices, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at Pokhara's finest restaurant — grilled fresh trout from Phewa Lake with roasted vegetables and Himalayan salad
meals.dinner: Return to resort for a private chef's table dinner experience — personalized 5-course tasting menu with wine pairing, served on your private terrace under the stars

day_by_day.notes: Phewa Lake is approximately 20 minutes from the resort by private vehicle. The International Mountain Museum is a must-visit for trekking and nature enthusiasts. October evenings can be cool — bring a light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Chartered helicopter tour of the Annapurna Circuit — fly over Annapurna Base Camp (4,130m), Thorong La Pass (5,416m), and the Kali Gandaki Gorge (world's deepest gorge). Land at a high-altitude clearing for champagne and panoramic Himalayan views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return by helicopter to Pokhara. Visit the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) perched on a hilltop above Phewa Lake — hike up or take a private jeep. Stunning 360-degree views of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges.
day_by_day.evening: Cultural evening experience — private performance of traditional Gurung and Tharu folk dances arranged exclusively for your group at the resort's amphitheater. Meet the performers and learn about the cultural significance of each dance.

meals.breakfast: Pre-flight breakfast at resort — continental spread with fresh pastries, yogurt parfait, seasonal fruits, and premium tea selection
meals.lunch: Champagne and gourmet canapés at high-altitude helicopter landing site — a truly once-in-a-lifetime dining experience
meals.dinner: Gala dinner at resort featuring a whole-roasted local lamb with Himalayan spice rub, accompanied by live traditional Sarangi music

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter tour is weather-dependent — October typically offers excellent flying conditions. Tour duration is approximately 3 hours. Warm layers and sunglasses essential at high altitude. Minimum advance booking required.

day_by_day.morning: Guided trek to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) — Day 1 of 2-day trek. Depart from Nayapul with private guide and luxury support team. Trek through Birethanti, Tikhedhunga, and Ulleri through terraced farmland and dense forests. Overnight at premium tea house or luxury tented camp at Chhomrong (2,170m).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Chhomrong village — explore this picturesque Gurung village with stunning views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli. Rest, acclimatize, and enjoy the mountain atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Campfire evening at Chhomrong with storytelling by your mountain guide about Himalayan legends and local folklore. Stargazing session with a telescope provided by the resort's adventure team.

meals.breakfast: Hearty packed breakfast from resort consumed at trailhead
meals.lunch: Freshly prepared hot lunch at a premium teahouse in Chhomrong — dal bhat with seasonal vegetables and local pickles
meals.dinner: Private chef-prepared dinner at luxury tented camp — pasta with Himalayan herbs, grilled chicken, and warm apple crumble dessert

day_by_day.notes: This is the beginning of the ABC trek — one of Nepal's most iconic routes. Total trekking distance today is approximately 14 km. Luxury porter service carries all heavy luggage. Guests carry only day packs with essentials.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure from Chhomrong — trek through Sinuwa, Bamboo, Dovan, and Himalaya Hotel. Pass through dense bamboo forests with possible wildlife sightings including Himalayan tahr and monal pheasant. Arrive at Machhapuchhre Base Camp (3,700m) for a rest and acclimatization break.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final ascent to Annapurna Base Camp (4,130m) — arrive at the iconic glacier amphitheater surrounded by 7,000m+ peaks including Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, and Machhapuchhre. Celebrate your achievement with a private champagne toast.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at ABC — witness the extraordinary alpenglow on the surrounding peaks. Warm dinner and overnight at premium ABC lodge. Hot water bottles provided for a comfortable night at altitude.

meals.breakfast: Hot porridge, eggs, and tea at Chhomrong camp before departure
meals.lunch: Hot soup, sandwiches, and energy snacks at Machhapuchhre Base Camp
meals.dinner: Premium dinner at ABC lodge — hearty mountain stew, fresh bread, and hot chocolate to warm up after the high-altitude experience

day_by_day.notes: Altitude at ABC is 4,130m — some guests may experience mild altitude sickness (headache, shortness of breath). Ascend slowly, stay hydrated, and inform your guide of any symptoms. Temperatures at night can drop to -5°C. Warm sleeping bags provided.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise at Annapurna Base Camp — one of the most spectacular mountain sunrises in the world. Early morning photography session with the resort's professional mountain photographer. Begin descent back toward Chhomrong.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue descent through Himalaya Hotel, Dovan, and Bamboo. The descent is significantly faster — approximately 5–6 hours total. Return to Nayapul and private vehicle transfer back to resort.
day_by_day.evening: Triumphant return to Aegean Bliss Resort — welcome back with a rose petal foot bath, cold towels, and celebratory drinks. Full body recovery massage at the spa to soothe trekking muscles.

meals.breakfast: Hot tea and light breakfast at ABC before descent
meals.lunch: Hot lunch at a teahouse in Bamboo — noodle soup, momos (dumplings), and fresh ginger tea
meals.dinner: Victory dinner at the resort's finest dining room — surf and turf featuring Himalayan trout and prime beef tenderloin with truffle sauce, accompanied by a bottle of premium Champagne

day_by_day.notes: Return day from ABC trek. Knees and quads will be tested on the descent — trekking poles highly recommended. The resort will have recovery amenities ready upon your return. Celebrate your achievement!

day_by_day.morning: Full rest day at the resort. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Optional gentle stretching or yoga session on the terrace. Spend the morning reading, journaling, or simply enjoying the stunning mountain views from your suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided visit to the Gupteshwor Mahadev Cave and Davis Falls in Pokhara — fascinating natural geological formations with mythological significance. Explore the cave's underground river and sacred Shiva shrine.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset photography walk along the Pokhara lakeside with a professional photographer guide. Learn composition techniques for capturing mountain landscapes and local life. Return to resort for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent brunch at resort — eggs cooked to order, waffles with Himalayan honey, fresh smoothie bowls, and premium coffee
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at resort — club sandwich, fresh salads, and tropical fruit platters
meals.dinner: Japanese-inspired omakase dinner at resort featuring Himalayan river fish sashimi, miso soup, and matcha desserts — a unique East-meets-Himalaya experience

day_by_day.notes: Recovery day is essential after the ABC trek. Listen to your body and avoid any strenuous activity. The resort's spa offers special post-trekking recovery packages including deep tissue massage and hydrotherapy.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided day hike to Sarangkot (1,592m) — a shorter but spectacular viewpoint above Pokhara with panoramic views of the entire Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. Optional paragliding experience from Sarangkot with a certified tandem instructor for the ultimate aerial perspective.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the old Pokhara Bazaar — a historic market area with traditional Newari architecture. Visit local artisan workshops producing hand-made paper (lokta), Thangka paintings, and silver jewelry. Private shopping experience with a cultural guide.
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class at the resort with the head chef — learn to prepare traditional Nepali dishes including dal bhat, momo dumplings, and sel roti. Enjoy your creations as dinner with paired beverages.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at resort before hike — energy-packed oatmeal, boiled eggs, fruit, and Nepali tea
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at Sarangkot viewpoint restaurant — wood-fired pizza and pasta with Himalayan views
meals.dinner: Dinner of dishes prepared during your personal cooking class — an authentic and personal culinary experience

day_by_day.notes: Paragliding from Sarangkot is a world-class experience — Pokhara is considered one of the top paragliding destinations globally. Flights last 20–30 minutes. October conditions are ideal with clear skies and favorable thermals. Must book in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided trek to Mardi Himal Base Camp viewpoint (3,500m) — a less-crowded alternative trek with exceptional views of Machhapuchhre and the Annapurna range. Trek through rhododendron forests and high alpine meadows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the High Camp area of Mardi Himal trek — stunning 360-degree views of the Himalayan panorama. Encounter local Gurung shepherds and their traditional yak herding practices. Begin descent back to lower elevations.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by private vehicle. Relaxing evening with a Himalayan herbal bath drawn by the resort's butler service. Pre-dinner drinks at the resort's sky bar.

meals.breakfast: Pre-trek breakfast at resort — French toast with Himalayan honey, fresh fruit salad, and strong Nepali coffee
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch enjoyed at High Camp viewpoint — smoked salmon wraps, cheese and crackers, fresh fruit, and hot soup
meals.dinner: Candlelit dinner on your private suite terrace — slow-braised yak stew with root vegetables, artisan bread, and a curated Himalayan cheese board

day_by_day.notes: Mardi Himal is a newer, less-commercialized trekking route offering a more intimate Himalayan experience. The trail is well-marked and suitable for fit trekkers. Total distance approximately 16 km. Luxury porter service provided.

day_by_day.morning: Private excursion to Begnas Lake — Pokhara's second-largest lake, quieter and more serene than Phewa Lake. Kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding on the pristine lake with views of forested hills. Birdwatching session with an ornithologist guide — spot kingfishers, egrets, and migratory birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bindyabasini Temple — one of Pokhara's most sacred Hindu temples dedicated to the goddess Bhagwati. Explore the surrounding old bazaar area and enjoy a guided cultural walk through historic Pokhara. Visit a traditional Thangka painting studio for a private demonstration.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell cocktail reception at the resort's panoramic terrace — celebrate the journey with fellow travelers and resort staff. Cultural performance by local musicians playing traditional Nepali instruments.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at resort — eggs florentine, fresh-baked croissants, seasonal fruit, and artisan teas
meals.lunch: Lakeside picnic at Begnas Lake — gourmet sandwiches, local cheeses, charcuterie, fresh fruit, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at the resort — 7-course Nepali-inspired tasting menu with premium wine pairing, featuring the best of Himalayan and international cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Begnas Lake is approximately 15 km from central Pokhara. The lake area is peaceful and less touristy — ideal for nature lovers. October is excellent for birdwatching as migratory species begin arriving.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise viewing from the resort terrace with hot Nepali tea and fresh pastries. Morning at leisure — last opportunity to enjoy the resort's spa, pool, and amenities. Optional final short walk through the resort's private garden trails.
day_by_day.afternoon: Checkout and private luxury transfer to Pokhara Airport or Kathmandu (by charter flight or helicopter). If time permits before departure, visit the Pokhara Regional Museum for a final cultural immersion into Nepalese history, art, and mountain heritage.
day_by_day.evening: If overnight in Kathmandu: check into a luxury heritage hotel (Dwarika's Hotel recommended). Evening heritage walk through Thamel and Durbar Square with a private guide — explore ancient temples, courtyards, and traditional Newari architecture.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — choose from the full menu as a farewell treat
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Pokhara airport lounge or en route to Kathmandu
meals.dinner: If in Kathmandu: dinner at Krishnarpan Restaurant at Dwarika's Hotel — Nepal's finest dining experience with a traditional Newari multi-course meal served in royal style

day_by_day.notes: Checkout time at resort is typically 12:00 noon. Arrange late checkout in advance if needed. Kathmandu evening activities are optional based on departure schedule. Dwarika's Hotel is a UNESCO-recognized heritage property.

day_by_day.morning: If in Kathmandu: early morning visit to Boudhanath Stupa — one of the world's largest Buddhist stupas and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Witness the morning puja (prayer ceremony) and circumambulate the stupa with monks. Visit Pashupatinath Temple — Nepal's most sacred Hindu temple complex on the banks of the Bagmati River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final shopping at premium Thamel boutiques — pick up last-minute souvenirs including pashmina shawls, Singing Bowls, Thangka art, and handcrafted jewelry. Private transfer to Tribhuvan International Airport for departure. VIP airport lounge access arranged.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Kathmandu — carry with you memories of the world's most magnificent mountain landscapes, rich cultural experiences, and the warm hospitality of the Nepali people.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Dwarika's Hotel or luxury hotel — traditional Newari breakfast with beaten rice, yogurt, and Nepali tea
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at Kathmandu's finest restaurant — OR airport lounge dining before departure
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport lounge dinner

day_by_day.notes: Final day — allow at least 3 hours before international departure for airport procedures. Keep essential medications, camera equipment, and valuables in carry-on luggage. Nepal's departure tax is included in most international tickets. Namaste and safe travels!

query: Nepal trekking Annapurna, $2000 solo, October 2026, 14 days
